LOO-593 · demo evidence · November 4, 2026

Desktop through the server

The embedded Loopflow library has been removed locally. Native Work reads, writes and subscriptions now use the server. Review the observed behavior and measured latency cost below. Final integration and publication are being handled by the Task’s live Graph; this page does not claim a finished gate or request shipping approval.

Built from the native demo record, raw measurements and methodology, and verification handoff.

Observed in the live app

The configured Codex conversation retained its unsent draft while the private server stopped. After recovery, it remembered LOO593-SERVER-814, reported the same directory, and accepted a rename through the server. Session and provider process IDs stayed unchanged.

Performance: a smaller client, added latency

Matched debug workloads on the same Mac: 31 sequential samples per path, warm statistics use the final 30. These measure protocol responses, not screen rendering.

OperationEmbedded median / p95Server median / p95
Roadmap read21.06 / 23.23 ms26.79 / 36.82 ms
Session rename50.68 / 54.47 ms87.60 / 123.74 ms
First subscription frame26.95 / 40.03 ms33.07 / 43.04 ms
Checkpoint16.61 / 19.48 ms22.00 / 28.63 ms

Desktop’s debug executable shrank from 282,749,312 to 57,519,360 bytes (about 270 to 55 MiB). The separate server still occupies memory: an idle five-second sample measured 246.7 MiB RSS and 0.19% of one CPU. No matched embedded memory sample exists.

Server readiness took 257 ms; one stop/start/read took 283 ms. These are single observations. Writes run the complete CLI; no second mutation executor was kept to conceal the cost.

Replay

  1. Open /Users/jack/.lf/demos/loo593-server-5r7obf0c/Loopflow Server Cutover.app. This is the isolated Live app. Expect the existing chat with its earlier marker.
  2. Enter an unsent draft. Stop and restart only this fixture’s server using its private Machine and identical bundled helper. Expect paused input while unavailable, automatic recovery and the same draft. Exact fixture paths and receipts are in the demo note; do not target the installed server.
  3. Submit the draft once. Expect preserved history and working directory. Rename with Cmd-K → Rename Session → Save; expect the server’s Session record to reflect the new name.

Failures and limits stay visible

The full headless Desktop suite found an uninitialized private-store fixture in PortfolioServiceTests. Its repair and final Xcode build remain with the live Graph. PR #1813 also requires reconciliation with main before publication.

Initial demo packaging failed on a missing framework path, a helper hash mismatch, and a long automation socket path. The fixture was repaired; these failures are retained in the Markdown record. The pictured app predates the separate pane-close race repair, which passed focused tests. This demonstration does not prove mobile integration, Linux replacement or a released-installation upgrade.

Review questions
